title: Check whether two words use the same letters
summary: Decide whether one bag of letter tiles can spell exactly the other bag's word, nothing extra and nothing missing.
goal: Decide whether the two bags hold exactly the same letters

examples.label: listen / silent
examples.explanation: Both bags hold e, i, l, n, s, t once each.

examples.label: rat / car
examples.explanation: The first bag has a t and no c; the second has a c and no t.

examples.label: Different sizes
examples.explanation: The bags hold different numbers of tiles.

ladder.name: Cross out matching tiles
ladder.idea: For each tile in the first bag, search the second bag for the same letter and cross it out.

ladder.name: Sort both words
ladder.idea: Sort the letters of each word and compare the results.
ladder.insight: Anagrams are the same letters in a different order, so putting both in the same order makes them identical.

ladder.name: One tally sheet
ladder.idea: Add one for every letter of the first word and subtract one for every letter of the second. Anagrams leave every count at zero.
ladder.insight: Order does not matter at all, only how many of each letter. Counting needs one pass and, for 26 letters, a fixed-size tally.

approaches.name: One tally sheet
approaches.summary: Add for the first word, subtract for the second, then check every count is zero.

transfer.problem: Can a ransom note be cut out of a magazine, using each magazine letter at most once?
transfer.explanation: Count the magazine's letters, then subtract the note's letters; if any count goes below zero, the note cannot be made.

selfCheck: Returns False straight away when the lengths differ.
Counts letters instead of comparing positions.
Checks that every count ends at exactly zero.
Handles repeated letters, such as "aab" and "aba".
